summary: Depressed mood and/or anhedonia plus associated sleep/appetite/concentration/energy/guilt/psychomotor/suicidality symptoms for 2+ weeks causing impairment; tracked with PHQ-9 (score >=10 suggests MDD, a 5-point drop = response, <5 = remission). USPSTF 2023 (Grade B): screen all adults 19+, including pregnant/postpartum; evidence is insufficient (I statement) for routine suicide-risk screening in the general adult population. VA/DoD 2022 (the current actionable US guideline - see guideline-currency flag in News) first-line: SSRI/SNRI/bupropion/mirtazapine/trazodone, plus newly added vilazodone and vortioxetine, with/without CBT, IPT, or newly added short-term psychodynamic therapy; adequate trial ~4-8 weeks; step 2 = augment (atypical antipsychotic, lithium, T3, or a second antidepressant) or switch; esketamine/ketamine or rTMS after 2+ failed adequate trials, which is how treatment-resistant depression (TRD) is defined. Guideline-currency flag: APA's only full MDD practice guideline remains the 3rd edition (Oct 2010, reaffirmed 2015), now filed under APA 'Legacy Practice Guidelines' - no newer full APA CPG exists.

news.what: Guideline-currency flag: no new full APA MDD practice guideline exists. APA's 3rd edition (Oct 2010, reaffirmed 2015) remains its only full CPG and is now listed under 'Legacy Practice Guidelines' - treat VA/DoD (2022) below as the current actionable US guideline, not APA.
SPRAVATO REMS modified (most recent update) - certified-setting dispensing and provider-monitoring requirements continue.
FDA approved Spravato (esketamine) as monotherapy for treatment-resistant depression; previously required a concomitant oral antidepressant.
Dextromethorphan-bupropion (Auvelity) approved for agitation associated with Alzheimer's dementia - a separate indication from MDD, not an MDD-label change.

drugs.warning: Class suicidality boxed warning; also dose-dependent seizure risk
Class suicidality boxed warning; serotonin syndrome risk with MAOIs and other serotonergic agents
Class suicidality boxed warning; contraindicated with MAOIs within 14 days (serotonin syndrome)
Boxed: increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; antidepressant-class suicidality warning also applies in the adjunct setting

drugs.line: 3L (TRD after 2+ failed trials; also MDD with acute suicidal ideation)
drugs.warning: Boxed: sedation, dissociation, abuse/misuse potential, suicidal thoughts and behaviors; REMS-restricted (certified settings only, monitoring incl. pulse oximetry for at least 2h post-dose)

notOnCard: Quetiapine XR (Seroquel XR) and brexpiprazole (Rexulti) - cut from the table above for the 8-agent space limit; both are adjunctive atypical antipsychotics carrying the same dementia-related-psychosis mortality boxed warning as aripiprazole

Zuranolone (Zurzuvae) and brexanolone (Zulresso) - both approved only for postpartum depression, not MDD; zuranolone received an FDA Complete Response Letter for a general-MDD indication, so neither gets a drug row here
Brexanolone commercial discontinuation (reported 2025-01-01) - Tier 4 only, no FDA notice located; omitted
Lumateperone (Caplyta) for MDD - unverified; referenced only in an APA practice-update snippet with no label pulled; omitted entirely
Trazodone, vilazodone, vortioxetine, lithium, and T3 augmentation - named in VA/DoD 2022 as options but no FDA label pulled this pass; no drug row
Ketamine (racemic, non-esketamine) and rTMS as TRD options - named in VA/DoD 2022 guideline text but no device/drug label pulled this pass; no row
